summary: Tool-adapter handshake causing synchronous wait and 2xx-3xx ms e2e amplification
summary_detail: Customer reports sudden increase in 95th/99th pct tail for requests that invoke external tool adapters. Problem appears after a recent validation-layer rollout that inserts a synchronous handshake to confirm tool metadata schemas.
description: Issue summary: Since 2026-03-11 23:00 UTC Acme Health is seeing elevated end-to-end latency on inference calls that result in tool/function calls. The increase is concentrated in p95/p99 and manifests as ~200-600ms extra per request. Impact: Production users experience slow responses for workflows that rely on tool calls (document fetch + structured output). Some user requests time out in client at 30s during heavy bursts. Environment: Production, us-west region, dedicated account for Acme Health (enterprise).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Acme Health integration with model redwood-7b-v2 pinned to version v2026-03-09
2) Issue a typical user prompt that triggers the 'patient_record_lookup' tool via tool-calling flow
3) Observe end-to-end timing in Redwood response stream and compare to baseline (before 2026-03-11)
4) Capture server-side trace for the request (trace-id from logs)
observed_behavior: Requests that include a tool call show an extra synchronous 'adapter handshake' step between serving-runtime and validation-service. This handshake blocks the token-generation stream while a schema confirmation RPC runs, adding ~180-420ms per call and sometimes cascading to retries and client-side timeouts.
expected_behavior: Tool-call validation should be async/non-blocking (prefetch/validate in parallel with token generation) or fast-path cached for known adapter schemas so token emission latency remains unchanged for warm schemas.

investigation_notes: Initial triage by Support: correlated with rollout of validation shim v1.4.2 to function-proxy on 2026-03-11 22:45 UTC. Trace analysis shows handshake is synchronous and not using local cache for schema ids. Hypothesis: validation-service call is performed inline with request path rather than as background preflight; cold-cache and remote KMS calls for signature verification amplify latency. Observed higher amplification in eu-central with slightly higher network RTT. No increased CPU or queue length on serving pods; latency spike originates from blocking RPC to validation-service. Related PRs flagged: function-proxy PR#501 introduced synchronous confirm_schema RPC.
action_items: 1) Roll back validation shim on function-proxy in us-west for Acme Health to v1.4.1 as a short-term mitigation
2) Implement a cached async validation path: check local schema cache and only call validation-service if cache miss
3) Add metrics for adapter-handshake latency and cache hit ratio to Console dashboard
4) Add an integration test exercising heavy concurrent tool-call flows to detect regressions
customer_updates: 2026-03-12 08:30 UTC - Support (Jamal): We have observed the latency amplification and are investigating. Asking for sample request ids from the customer.
2026-03-12 09:12 UTC - Customer (Acme Health, T. Morgan): Provided three trace ids and confirmed issue reproduces on their staging mirror.

2026-03-12 13:45 UTC - Support (Priya): We began a controlled rollback for the validation shim in us-west for your dedicated pool. Expect improvement within 10 minutes. Will follow up with post-rollback metrics.
2026-03-12 14:05 UTC - Customer: Observed improved p95 by ~340ms after rollback. Thanks.
engineering_notes: Eng found that the validation-service endpoint validates full schema payload including signature verification against KMS which can take 150-500ms on cold paths. function-proxy change made this inline for simplicity; need to decouple. Proposed fix in serving-runtime: spawn non-blocking validation coroutine and proceed with best-effort token streaming; if validation fails later, trigger compensating action (fallback to safe-output or call error hook). PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2151
temporary_workaround: Rollback function-proxy to v1.4.1 for impacted dedicated pools OR pin customer's routes to the cached-schema variant. Customers can also increase client timeout as a stopgap but not recommended.
resolution: Mitigation: Rolled back validation shim for Acme Health in us-west on 2026-03-12 13:50 UTC. Observed p95 improved ~320ms within 5-10 minutes. Long-term fix: engineering will publish an async cached validation flow in function-proxy and serving-runtime. Target for merged fix: PR#2151, scheduled for canary rollout 2026-03-16.
notes: Keep ticket open until PR#2151 has been canaried and p95/p99 metrics return to baseline for Acme Health for 72h. Escalation path: if reoccurence reported, promote to P0 and trigger incident bridge.
